New Novitec N-Largo Ferrari 12Cilindri Is THE Exotic Grand Tourer To Crave
21 photos
Photo: Novitec
With the 12Cilindri being Ferrari’s modern entry in the front mid-engine and rear-wheel drive stable, it is no wonder that certain tuners have launched all kinds of upgrades for this model ever since it became available some two years ago.
Novitec’s name is definitely on the list, as it has already introduced a few takes on this model. Fast forward to this week, though, and the renowned tuner now has the so-called N-Largo bundle available. Created in partnership with German designer Vittorio Strosek, just like other N-Largo projects introduced over the years, the extras are all about aerodynamic function, in addition to the enhanced design, and they definitely help the model stand out from the crowd much easier.
Well, assuming that you know your Ferrari 12Cilindris , that is, because the upgrades will definitely fly under the radar for the average Joe. But then again, this is what Novitec is famously known for, and that’s crafting all kinds of fine projects that do not go anywhere near the brash realm. And that’s why we (or I, in this case) adore their builds, because Novitec can easily host a tuning course for other tuners. And it’s been extremely hard not to mention Mansory’s name here. Wait a minute...
The N-Largo version of the Ferrari 12Cilindri benefits from larger wheel arches at the front and rear. The fender flares have made the supercar (it’s actually an exotic GT, as mentioned above) much wider than before. According to Novitec, the modded 12Cilindri in question is (almost) 3 inches (7 cm) wider at the front and 5 inches (13 cm) wider at the rear.
Photo: Novitec Rocker panels between the wide fenders are also on deck, and they make the car more aerodynamic. The carbon covers for the door mirrors contribute to the racy look of the car . There are also large air intakes at the front, an integrated spoiler that reduces the nose-lift at high speeds, and a new hood with integrated and carbon-framed air outlets that provide a view of the two red intake manifolds of the V12, which also optimizes the engine bay’s heat dissipation.
Additional upgrades include the ducktail spoiler at the rear, with its three-piece design, which has been integrated into the N-Largo widebody kit. A dry carbon diffuser can also be seen at the rear, as well as two dual tailpipe tips at the left and right, which are part of the tuner’s sports exhaust system. This component features butterfly valves, and Novitec also offers a version with 999 fine-gold plating for a more exclusive look, which also improves the heat dissipation. The sports catalysts are optional.
The special makeover does not end here, because the Ferrari 12Cilindri N-Largo by Novitec also benefits from new wheels. Made in partnership with Vossen, they are called the Novitec NF12 N-Largo, and they measure 12x22 inches at the rear and 10x21 inches at the front, wrapped in 325/30 and 275/35 tires respectively. Courtesy of the Novitec sports springs, the vehicle rides roughly inches (30 mm) closer to the ground.
Now, the new exhaust system likely allows the engine to produce a bit more oomph, but since the upgrade is not significant at all, Novitec hasn’t mentioned the revised output and thrust. But even without any outside intervention, the mill, which is a naturally aspirated V12, in case you forgot, with a 6.5-liter displacement, is very potent.
Photo: Novitec The output is 818 hp (830 ps/610 kW ) and the thrust stands at 500 pound-feet (678 Nm) of torque, as per the model’s official spec sheet. This allows the Ferrari 12Cilindri to reach 62 mph (100 kph) in just 2.9 seconds, and flat-out, it will do up to 211 mph (340 kph) wherever the road and legislation allow it.
Novitec offers the N-Largo Ferrari 12Cilindri as a complete package, including the supercar, but alternatively, it will also convert vehicles to this configuration upon request. Therefore, interested parties must reach out to them to discuss the details, including the finances, because the money haven’t been mentioned in the press release. And if you find out how much it costs, then feel free to drop a line below and share this information with us.
In the meantime, we will remind you that Ferrari’s 12Cilindri hit the assembly line at Maranello, Italy, in 2024. It is the successor to the 812 Superfast, which replaced the F12berlinetta in the Prancing Horse’s stable, and the latter succeeded the 599. It is 186.2 inches (4,730 mm) long, 85.7 inches (2,176 mm) wide, and 50.8 inches (1,290 mm) tall. The wheelbase measures 106.3 inches (2,700 mm), and the car has a curb weight of over 3,400 pounds (1,560 kg).
Two body styles are available, a two-door berlinetta (coupe) and a two-door retractable hardtop convertible, and both feature the same front mid-engine and rear-wheel drive layout, and pack the same old-school naturally aspirated 6.5-liter V12 engine, mated to an eight-speed DCT , in the same configuration.
